messages:
Amanda: Heads-up — onboarding a new HF chat_template for the Falcon trial. When we convert to Redwood prompt the converter sometimes inserts an empty assistant block and duplicates the system sentinel, which shifts the KV-cache. Example jinja snippet I got from the model repo:
```jinja
- role: system
  content: "{% if system %}{{ system }}{% endif %}"
- role: user
  content: "{{ user }}"
- role: assistant
  content: "{{ assistant|default('') }}"
```
Amanda: Rendered by the HF->Redwood tool it becomes (trimmed):
```
<<SYS>>Welcome to Falcon<<SYS>><<SYS>><<SYS>>
User: Hello
Assistant: 
```
Amanda: See the duplicated <<SYS>> and the blank Assistant line — that blank assistant seems to get turned into an explicit message and causes the runtime to treat the next user tokens as continuation, breaking KV alignment.
Raj: Hmm, can you paste the exact converter command you used?
Amanda: `python tools/convert_chat.py --input model_chat_template.json --out redwood_prompt.txt`
Oliver: I think this is the classic jinja-empty-vs-undefined issue. `default('')` will render an empty string which HF's chat schema may interpret as an assistant message. Try `{{ assistant | default(omit) }}` is not valid jinja, but `({% if assistant is defined and assistant %}...{% endif %})` will omit the role entirely.
Raj: Good call. Also check whether tokenizer special tokens are configured in `config.json` — some models include "eos_token": "" and the converter maps that to our sentinel. If converter sees consecutive sentinels it doesn't dedupe.
ml-bot: Known issue #412: converter treats any assistant role present in the template as a literal role even if empty. It adds a sentinel like `"<|assistant|>"`. There's a suggested patch in the ticket to skip roles with empty/whitespace-only content.
Oliver: Quick patch suggestion: in convert_chat.py, when you iterate messages, do `content = message.get('content','')
if content.strip() == '': continue` — that removes blank assistant blocks.
Amanda: Before we change converter, can we validate whether removing blank assistant blocks changes evaluation results? We saw a slight quality regression in quant tests but weren't sure if it came from this.
Raj: I'll run a small eval on the regression suite — 50 prompts. Command I'll use: `python eval/run_eval.py --model redwood-falcon-test --prompts tests/kv_alignment_prompts.json --convert-tool tools/convert_chat.py`
Raj: ETA ~20m, I'll post numbers here. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
Amanda: Thanks. If this is the culprit it's high priority — misaligned KV cache can silently corrupt long-form outputs.
ml-bot: Related note: the runtime also recognizes explicit system tokens from tokenizers. If model config uses `add_bos=true` plus a system token string, converter needs to avoid inserting an extra bos. Otherwise you can get double-prefixes.
Oliver: Another defensive approach: change converter to emit an annotated comment in the prompt when it drops a role, e.g., `<!-- dropped empty assistant -->` so audits can see what happened.
Amanda: Agreed. Raj please include a run with both converter versions (current vs skip-empty). If regression disappears with skip-empty then we merge fix + add unit test.
Raj: Will do. tagging @Oliver for the small patch and @Amanda for rollout plan.
Amanda: Perfect. I'll also add a checklist item to onboarding docs: "avoid `assistant|default('')` in jinja; prefer conditional omission."
Oliver: quick lgtm on the patch naming: `convert_chat: skip-empty-roles` -> small PR after Raj's tests. :thumbsup:
Raj: Update: first 10 prompts done — metric delta looks like +0.7 BLEU (better) when skipping empty assistant. Running remaining 40 now.
Amanda: Nice, thanks. Keep updates here and we'll follow up with eng-runtime once Raj confirms.
